25e1a1e9-166d-4195-972e-51f9ef3369b7.quote: Maco's loadout is Exarch, paired with Revelation and Fervour — the Empowerment Support build. Exarch's major turns every heal or shield he lands into a short buff for that ally, extra attack speed and bonus on-hit magical damage, fitting a kit built around flexing Gift! between healing and hurting; Revelation also trims his ability cooldowns on cast, and Fervour turns his basic attacks into passive team healing. It trades away pure protection, like extra healing received, for rewarding his own aggression — the fit for a support who closed the Inner Tower fight at 27.8 with a personal double kill.

25e1a1e9-166d-4195-972e-51f9ef3369b7.quote: Kira's loadout is Vermis, with Serration and Melting Point — the Auto-Attack / Anti-Tank build. Vermis's major hits every third consecutive basic attack on the same hero for bonus damage based on their max health, rewarding sustained fire on one target, while Melting Point adds extra damage against anyone stacking more than 125 physical armor and Serration adds bonus damage tied to the target's missing health once the major procs. It's an all-offense loadout with no defensive minor at all, so it leans entirely on teammates to peel the enemy's Bayle and Grux engage away from her while she keeps her attacks landing.

25e1a1e9-166d-4195-972e-51f9ef3369b7.quote: The loadout here is Thraex, with Savage Strikes and Ferocity — the Sustained Duelist build. Thraex's major marks whoever Scarlett last basic-attacked, boosting her damage to them and cutting what they deal back, rewarding a hero who stays on target through a long fight. Savage Strikes adds flat bonus damage that triples against heroes, and Ferocity stacks attack speed the longer she's in a fight, both compounding the longer the skirmish runs — a fit for a jungle matchup that read favored from start to finish, trading away the burst tools a shorter pick-style fight would want.

25e1a1e9-166d-4195-972e-51f9ef3369b7.quote: Argus's loadout is Vesh, with The Tenth Seal and Mind Rot — the Ability Damage Mage build; the major turns every landed ability into a damage-over-time tick worth a share of the hit, scaling up the longer the game runs, which suits a poke-heavy kit built around Dread Nova and Particle Shredder. Mind Rot adds bonus damage tied to the target's current health so it still bites into a tankier body like Grux, and The Tenth Seal strengthens the ultimate once he hits level 10. None of the three pieces offer any defense, a bet that the poke and the DoT outlast the enemy rather than needing to survive their engage, and one that didn't pay off on the deaths that fed the mid and late-game objectives.
